senses.definition: come upon unexpectedly or after searching
examples: found art
the lost-and-found department

senses.definition: food and lodging provided in addition to money
examples: they worked for $30 and found

senses.definition: come upon, as if by accident; meet with
examples: We find this idea in Plato
I happened upon the most wonderful bakery not very far from here
She chanced upon an interesting book in the bookstore the other day

senses.definition: set up or found
examples: She set up a literacy program

senses.definition: discover or determine the existence, presence, or fact of by perception with the eyes
examples: She detected high levels of lead in her drinking water
We found traces of lead in the paint

senses.definition: set up or lay the groundwork for
examples: establish a new department

senses.definition: come upon after searching; find the location of something that was missed or lost
examples: Did you find your glasses?
I cannot find my gloves!

senses.definition: use as a basis for; found on
examples: base a claim on some observation

senses.definition: establish after a calculation, investigation, experiment, survey, or study
examples: find the product of two numbers
The physicist who found the elusive particle won the Nobel Prize

senses.definition: come to believe on the basis of emotion, intuitions, or indefinite grounds
examples: I feel that he doesn't like me
I find him to be obnoxious
I found the movie rather entertaining

senses.definition: perceive or be contemporaneous with
examples: We found Republicans winning the offices
You'll see a lot of cheating in this school
The 1960's saw the rebellion of the younger generation against established traditions
I want to see results

senses.definition: get something or somebody for a specific purpose
examples: I found this gadget that will serve as a bottle opener
I got hold of these tools to fix our plumbing
The chairman got hold of a secretary on Friday night to type the urgent letter

senses.definition: make a discovery, make a new finding
examples: Roentgen discovered X-rays
Physicists believe they found a new elementary particle

senses.definition: obtain through effort or management
examples: She found the time and energy to take care of her aging parents
We found the money to send our sons to college

senses.definition: decide on and make a declaration about
examples: find someone guilty

senses.definition: receive a specified treatment (abstract)
examples: These aspects of civilization do not find expression or receive an interpretation
His movie received a good review
I got nothing but trouble for my good intentions

senses.definition: perceive oneself to be in a certain condition or place
examples: I found myself in a difficult situation
When he woke up, he found himself in a hospital room

senses.definition: get or find back; recover the use of
examples: She regained control of herself
She found her voice and replied quickly

senses.definition: succeed in reaching; arrive at
examples: The arrow found its mark

senses.definition: accept and make use of one's personality, abilities, and situation
examples: My son went to Berkeley to find himself
